cqa_tuples.knowledge_point: The student names at least four distinct mobile routing challenges from the catalog.
cqa_tuples.target_criteria: FULL = at least 4 distinct valid challenges named; PARTIAL = 1..3; ABSENT = 0
cqa_tuples.source_rubric_span: Naming any 2 valid challenges (1 mark). Catalog: Adaptation, Security, MAC, QoS, Scalability, Power.

cqa_tuples.knowledge_point: The student provides a valid description for the first chosen challenge.
cqa_tuples.target_criteria: any of: dynamic topology/node movement for Adaptation; packet interception/injection for Security; signal interference/collisions for MAC; topology/resource constraints for QoS; increasing network size for Scalability; battery-powered optimization for Power Consumption.
evidence_facets: Adaptation: dynamic positioning or node mobility
Medium Access Control: signal interference or collisions
Quality of Service: topology changes or resource constraints
cqa_tuples.partial_credit_rule: Partial descriptions that capture the core mechanism earn 0.75 marks.
cqa_tuples.source_reference_span: 1.Adaptation: The network has to handle the dynamic positioning of the nodes/topology changes. 2.Security: Interception of packets or injection of faulty packages is easily possible. 3.Medium Access Control: Wireless networks feature new possibilities for inference and collisions. 4.Quality of Service: Due to the rapidly changing network topology, imprecise network information, and resource constraints. 5.Scalability: It is vital that routing protocols are capable of dealing with increasing network sizes. 6.Power Consumption: As most mobile devices are battery-powered, power consumption becomes an important optimization factor.
